steps.text:
this site is home to the original variant of chess called ”token chess” or simply ”token.” 
  
 here you can learn the game and play online, or against [Fairy Stockfish](https://fairy-stockfish.github.io/).
this tutorial explains the concept of the game, and contains instructions for using available features.
if you're familiar with chess variants, [start here](/tutorials/token).

standard-rules.title: The game of chess...
standard-rules.quote: “The game of chess is a lake in which a mosquito can bathe and an elephant can drown.” – Indian Proverb

steps.text:
Chess is a board game that has been played for roughly half a millenium. 
 To learn the basics of the game, [lichess.org](https://lichess.org/learn) is a great comprehensive source.

In understanding the concept of chess *variants*, it helps to know that chess itself is a European *variation* of a type of board game that has existed for around 1,000 years longer than modern chess. The original game, [Chaturanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaturanga), spread to other regions and evolved into [Makruk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makruk), [Shogi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shogi), and many other variations. These variations have different pieces and rules, but share the concept of a coordinate system and a set of movable figures, one of which must be protected. 
 Below is a game of [Xiangqi.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi)

fairy-chess.title: Strange characters...
fairy-chess.quote: “We do these things for ourselves alone.” – Thomas Rayner Dawson, fairy chess composer

steps.text: “Fairy Chess“ is a general term for a chess variant that includes nonstandard piece types, or “fairy pieces.“

Below is a [variant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knighted_chess) imagined by third world chess champion José Raúl Capablanca. 
 Note the unorthodox 10x8 board and the addition of two fairy pieces.

It was popular in some historical chess communities to include fairy pieces in chess compositions. 
 The puzzle below was composed in 1911 by [Thomas Rayner Dawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Rayner_Dawson), a prolific fairy chess composer. 
 It involves a fairy piece which combines the movement of a Rook and a Knight.
steps.note: White to move, mate in two.

token.title: Token Chess
token.quote: “The ~~pawn~~ token is the soul of chess.” – François-André Danican Philidor

steps.text: this variant adds a peculiar collection of fairy pieces and a **draft system** to the normal rules of chess.

before the game begins, each player chooses their starting setup, oblivious to their opponent's choices. every piece has a price, and players have 39 tokens to spend.

you can use the built-in drafts to [play a game](/play), or sign up to make your own. 

for the rules of drafting, see the [next section](/tutorials/draft).

To create a draft, sign up and log in to a Token Chess account. Then click on the 'My Drafts' button in the top right corner. Here you can create and save up to 5 drafts for playing games. Simply drag pieces from the pallette onto the first two ranks of the board-- the first rank is for pieces, the second rank is for Pawns, Painters, and Snares.

**In order to play a multiplayer game, one of your drafts must be set as 'Active' using the button on the drafts page.** 
 This draft, highlighted in green at the top, will be your starting setup when playing a game, and may be changed at any time between games. **Make sure to save any changes made to a draft with the button at the bottom!**

There are special restrictions on the **quantity** of each piece type in a draft. This is designed to keep things fun and fair by promoting diversity and mitigating 'hordes' of a single piece type. For example, while a single Painter is a formidable foe, eight of them together are...*oppressive.*

Just like token values, these quantity restrictions are a work in progress and may change in response to community feedback.

As of **January 2026**, the quantity limit for each piece is as follows:

| Max Allowed | Pieces |
|-------------|--------|
| **1** | Archer, Painter |
| **2** | Amazon, Champion, Princess, Queen |
| **3** | Rook, Wizard |
| **4** | Bishop, Knight, Baker, Snare |

**Please note:** These limits are **per-piece**. For example, you may include *both* a Painter *and* an Archer in the same draft.

Once you have saved and activated at least one draft, you are ready to play a game of Token! At the top menu, click Play -> Game Lobby. Here you can create a game room with a time control of your liking, or join another player's room by clicking their username.

Each room has a code, so you can alternatively join a friend's game by clicking Play -> Join Game and entering their room code. Once in a room, you can rematch as many times as you like, with the option to switch your active draft in between each game of the match.

Multiplayer is currently the **only** supported playing method, as there is no Token Chess AI yet. 
 For fans of computer chess - stay tuned!

If your game starts from the default chess position, it means one of two things: **1) you or your opponent do not have a draft set as 'active'**, or **2) you or your opponent are using a draft that became illegal after balance changes**. If the second case happens, check the balance notes at the bottom of this page, then remove and re-add any pieces in your draft that have increased in value.

Click the 'Board' option at the top menu to use the Board Editor and Analysis feature. Here you can create custom positions by dragging pieces onto the board. You can also copy/edit/paste FEN in the text bar on the bottom. To enter analysis mode, press **Analyze.**
Once in analysis mode, you can freely play moves from both sides. Forward and rewind through moves using the buttons on the side, or with your arrow keys.

Access puzzles by clicking Play -> Puzzles. This feature is a work in progress, as there are only a few haphazard puzzles currently available. In the future, this will host a collection of community-created puzzles of various difficulties.

Token Chess is created and maintained by Nathaniel Clizbe, a software developer and chess enthusiast. 
 Source code for the project is available [here.](https://github.com/cliz1/tokenchess)

This project is developed as an experimental chess platform; bugs and unfinished features may exist. 
 Issues and suggestions are welcome via GitHub.
This platform itself does not yet host any social features. To discuss the game or find opponents, join our [lichess team!](https://lichess.org/team/token-club)
As this game has some novel aspects, it is strongly encouraged to share your experience or suggest ideas!

May 2026: 
 **1) Wizard token cost 4 -> 7**. 
 Fairy stockfish has revealed the tactical potency of this piece, and will consistently favor it over a Rook and Pawn. 
 Don't buy it? Give Fairy stockfish a Wizard and find out! 
 **2) Archer token cost 7 -> 5** 
 While this piece seems unbeatable at first glance, it takes some effort to prove its value. In an endgame, this piece becomes a lot worse, and due to its low range it is likely worth no more than a Rook. But certainly not more than two Bishops! 
 **3) Snare token cost 2 -> 1** 
 The Snare cannot capture, and is very weak to attack by Pawns. Giving it a valuation of more than a Pawn seems unfair for this reason. 
 **4) Rolling Snare Movement buff** 
 The Rolling Snare now moves like a Queen to make it more comparable to Pawn/Painter promotions.

It is nearly impossible to survive more than a few moves against an Amazon in endgame play. 
 In a more advanced example below, the Amazon swiftly overcomes a Champion with a beautiful *zugzwang*.

In the event of stalemate, if the side delivering the stalemate has a General, the result is a win for that side rather than a draw. Interestingly, this allows a General to win by itself against another.
steps.note: In this diagram, black is forced into a corner, after which the stalemate wins for white.

Champion.title: Champion
Champion.quote: “Suffer now and live the rest of your life as a champion.” – Muhammad Ali

steps.text: The Rook-Knight, an ancient fairy piece, was first called *Campione* by the priest [Pietro Carerra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pietro_Carrera).
steps.note: Capture the Knight in two moves.

steps.text: The Champion provides a special haven for the King, just as the Rook does.

Princess.title: Princess
Princess.quote: “Whoever makes me unhappy for a day, I will make suffer for a lifetime.” – Empress Dowager Cixi

steps.text: The Princess possess the strengths of Bishop and Knight without any of the weaknesses.

Amazon.title: Amazon
Amazon.quote: “I will not be triumphed over.” – Cleopatra VII

steps.text:
Behold!

The all-powerful hybrid they call the [Amazon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazons). 

Some say she is too powerful for the 8x8 dimension. 
Is it true? 

Find out yourself, if you have the tokens...

Baker.title: Baker
Baker.quote: “All sorrows are less with bread.” – Sancho Panza

steps.text:
The King and the Baker are distinct only by blood. 

The latter's fate has no significance to the game of chess, but don't be fooled - they are no less valuable than a Bishop or Knight. 

Unlike those pieces, the Baker can checkmate solely with the help of their own King.
With a loyal Baker at his side, the King has little to fear.
steps.note: A mere Queen is not enough to break through this sturdy loaf maker.

Painter.title: Painter
Painter.quote: “I dream my paintings, and then I paint my dreams.” – Vincent van Gogh

steps.text:
While similar to a Pawn, a Painter is incapable of violence - they are a dreamer, not a fighter. 

Rather than capture, the Painter *paints* pieces.
steps.note: That Rook could use a fresh coat...

steps.text:
Even when [promoting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotion_(chess)), the Painter refuses to pick up a sword. 
 
Instead, they become a *Royal Painter*, moving like a Queen, paintbrush still in hand.

A Painter cannot apply a new coat to a piece whose paint is still wet. 
 
 **When a piece is painted, it cannot be painted again on the opponent's next move.** 
 
 The piece may only be painted again once the paint dries one turn later.
steps.note: Sorry black, the paint is wet. Checkmate.

steps.text: The Snare cannot capture. It paralyzes any piece **directly next to or in front of it.**
steps.note: Step forward to ensnare the Rooks.

steps.text:
The Snare moves forward one square, 
straight or diagonally. 

It is worth no more than a single Pawn, but even pieces of the highest class may fall into its clutches.
steps.note: Ensnare the Queen and steal it with a Pawn.

steps.text:
The Snare poses no threat on its own. 
It gives no checks.

Putting the enemy in a cage, however, makes checkmate an easy task.

When promoting, it becomes a *Rolling Snare*. 

It moves any distance, and also traps pieces directly *behind* it.

Wizard.title: Wizard
Wizard.quote: “A wizard is never late. Nor is he early. He arrives precisely when he means to.” – Gandalf

steps.text:
The Wizard moves one or two squares as a Queen, but he is not bound by the regular laws of space. 

If an object stands between him and his destination, he simply teleports there.
steps.note: Capture the Queen in two moves.

steps.text:
The Wizard can **swap places** with a friendly piece within its movement range. 

His magic doesn't expose his King for an instant.
He may even rescue his King from inevitable defeat.

Archer.title: Archer
Archer.quote: “Swift as the wind, silent as the forest.” – Sun Tzu

steps.text:
The Archer was supposed to be a Bishop, but it flunked out of the priesthood. 

Still bound by birth to one square color, it can only move a single square at a time.

Failed by fate, the Archer chose a new path. They aquired the unthinkable ability to capture without moving. 

Pieces **2 to 3 diagonal squares away** from the Archer stand no chance.

General.title: General
General.quote: ”If the flying general of Dragon City were here, no Tartar steed would dare cross the Yin mountains.” –Wang Changling

steps.text:
In Xiangqi, the royal piece is traditionally carved with Shuài 帥 or Jiàng 將, both meaning ”General.” 

In Token, the King can optionally be replaced by this piece.

The General moves one square straight, 
**never diagonally.** 

As a result, the King dominates it one-on-one.
The General has a special [flying style](https://www.xiangqi.com/history), enabling him to *capture* like a Rook.
